Here are three reusable “Where is my order?” reply templates you can copy‑paste and edit with the relevant details:

---

**Template 1 – Standard Status Update**
> Hi **[Customer Name]**,  
> Thanks for your patience! Your order #[Order #] is currently **[current status]** (e.g., “in transit” or “out for delivery”).  
> You can track it here: **[tracking link]**.  
> If you have any other questions, just let me know.  

---

**Template 2 – Delayed Order with ETA**
> Hello **[Customer Name]**,  
> I’m sorry to let you know that your order #[Order #] is experiencing a slight delay. We expect it to arrive by **[estimated delivery date]** (estimated delivery window: **[date range]**).  
> You can view the latest updates here: **[tracking link]**.  
> Please feel free to reach out if you need anything else.  

---

**Template 3 – Order Confirmed & Ready to Ship**
> Hi **[Customer Name]**,  
> Great news! Your order #[Order #] has been **[packed/processed]** and will be shipped today. You’ll receive a tracking link shortly, or you can check it now: **[tracking link]**.  
> Delivery is expected **[delivery date]** (estimated **[delivery window]**).  
> Thanks for shopping with Kettle & Crumb!  

---

Just replace the bracketed placeholders with the actual order details, and you’ll have a ready‑to‑send reply each time. Let me know if you need anything else!

> Hey **[Customer Name]**,

> Let me know if there’s anything else I can help with!

attempts.text:
I’d pick **Template 2** — the delayed-order one — assuming there’s a confirmed delay.

It’s the most apologetic without being overly formal, and it gives an ETA, which is usually what a customer who’s written twice is really waiting for.

For a repeat contact, I’d tweak it slightly:  
*“Hey [Name], sorry for the repeat chasing — your order #[Order #] is running a bit behind…”*

But between the three, **Template 2** is the safer choice for a twice-written customer. If there’s no delay, I’d switch to **Template 1**. And since I can’t check your systems, I’d need the order details to confirm which one actually applies.
